The 'reach per post 7.77 all-time vs 2.76 over the last 14d' comparison is confounded by POSTING VOLUME, not by time. Volume-band read, real posts only (provider_post_id IS NOT NULL, insights-backed), mature days Aug 22-Sep 9 (all >=12d old so reach has settled): 1 post/day -> total 11.2/day, 11.2 per post; 2/day -> 17.3 / 8.7; 3-4/day -> 22.8 / 6.5; 5-9/day -> 22.3 / 3.0. Total reach SATURATES at ~22 impressions/day by 3-4 posts/day; per-post reach falls 4x across those bands. r(posts/day, per-post reach) = -0.775 over 22 days.

Why it is not a decline: the OLDEST, most-mature high-volume days (Aug 26-30, 8-9 posts/day) show per-post reach 2.25-3.0 -- the SAME as the recent low per-post numbers -- while the newer LOW-volume days (Sep 6-9, 1 post/day) show 11-13. Age works AGAINST the declining reading: if reach accumulated with time the oldest days would read highest, and they read lowest.

Consequence for the 09-28 gate: the binding constraint is a ~22 impressions/day REACH CEILING, not a downward trend. No production change can pass the engagement leg, and the configured cadence (posts_per_day=3, max_posts_per_day=3) already sits AT the saturation knee, so neither more nor fewer posts moves total reach. Keep cadence; the pivot candidate stays DISTRIBUTION/REACH.
